messages:
maya: Hey team — just got an escalation from ACME: multiple customers reported intermittent 429s and long tail latency during a batch ingest yesterday. They say it started after a client-side change around 21:10 UTC. Support ticket attached with sample request IDs.

sam: putting the ticket link in the thread. customer claims they weren't spiking above their committed volume so they think it's a burst/quota issue.

maya: exact quote: 'we see 429s for some requests and orders of magnitude higher p95 for generation calls (2.3s -> 7s). keys are rotating every 30s on their side for security reasons.'

ajay: key rotation every 30s can create auth storms — every time they rotate we see a flurry of new tokens hitting our auth service and possibly creating many short-lived sessions. That can blow up connection churn and trigger backend throttles.

lina: I pulled logs for the time window. We do see a spike in token-verification ops and an increase in TCP connection churn to the ingress ELBs. Also saw a burst in KV cache misses for model prefixes (lots of fresh sessions).

ops-bot: deploy/ingress: noticed a 3x increase in upstream 429s between 21:08-21:18 UTC. Average request size and seq lengths were similar.

ajay: can we reproduce quickly in the lab? We need to validate whether our rate limiter is per-key, per-client-ip, or per-account when tokens rotate. Also check the burst window params: token bucket size, refill rate, and per-route concurrency gates.

maya: customer provided a small repro: they rotate token and send 5 concurrent requests on each rotation. Over 30s, that's ~300 requests. Not huge, but concentrated. They reported the errors only for generation endpoints (chat and completions), not embeddings.

sam: suggested repro steps to customer: 1) run single-threaded client rotating token every 30s, 2) log x-request-id for failed calls, 3) capture timestamps. They returned logs showing repeated 401s from our auth node then 429s from the router.

ajay: hypothesis: auth layer returns transient 401 while verifying new token -> client retries with new token -> router sees a sudden burst from same account but different auth values -> our per-token limiter doesn't aggregate to account-level, so each new token gets an initial burst allowance. Combined, that exceeds account burst capacity and trips account-level fallback which emits 429.

lina: i can run a controlled experiment with our internal harness. Plan: emulate rotating tokens every 30s with N concurrent requests per rotation and sweep RPM/TPM and burst sizes. Use k6 to simulate. Example k6 snippet:```javascript
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function () {
  const token = generateRotatingToken(); // stub
  const params = { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } };
  for (let i=0;i<5;i++) {
    http.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/completions', JSON.stringify({prompt:'x'}), params);
  }
  sleep(30);
}```

ajay: nice. Also add a control that uses a single static token to confirm it's rotation-specific. Capture metrics: 429 count, 401 auth failures, p50/p95/p99 latencies, x-quota-remaining, and router reject reasons.

maya: customer also mentioned billing anomalies — some requests billed even though they got 429. Need to verify meter behavior: we should not bill on rejected responses.

lina: for the bench i'll toggle two configurations: current production rate-limiter and a proposed conservative default. Current: per-token bucket 20 TPS burst=40, per-account aggregate window 600 RPM, burst multiplier 2x. Proposed: per-account RPM default 3000 TPM=50000 burst-window 10s token-bucket size 200. (will run sweep).

ajay: please don't use those exact numbers in the public docs. For the experiment, let's parameterize: RPM sweep [100, 500, 1000, 3000], TPM sweep [1000, 10000, 50000], burst sizes [10,50,200]. We'll look for the knee where 95th latency > 2s or 5% 429s.

sam: can we also simulate NAT pooling effects? Many of customer's clients come through a small set of egress IPs and that changes connection reuse. If the kernel is ephemeral, ELB may open new connections frequently which increases server CPU for TLS handshakes.

lina: yes will add nginx/ELB connection churn by forcing short keepalive and new TCP per request in a subset of runs.

deploy-bot: note: staging cluster has a rolling deploy in 2h — avoid heavy runs that could affect other teams.

ajay: good call — we'll use the isolated load lab (traffic-isolated) between 02:00-04:00 UTC. I'll schedule it and ping oncall.

maya: for the immediate customer-facing reply: suggest they temporarily increase token reuse (if they can) or stagger rotations to smooth rate. Also offer a canary change: enable account-level aggregation so rotating tokens are counted under one account bucket instead of per-token buckets. That requires infra change but we can offer an alternative: a short-lived policy override for them (support-assisted bump) until we roll a fix.

sam: i'll draft the support note: ask them to run the k6 script with static token vs rotating token, capture headers x-request-id, x-rate-limit, x-quota-remaining, and send us a p95 hang. Also offer a temporary quota bump while we run the repro.

lina: experiment started — first run looks promising: static token at RPM=1000 TPM=10000 saw no 429s, rotating token with same aggregate rate triggered account 429s when burst size >50.

ajay: that confirms aggregation gap. Next step: reproduce with a policy change in load-lab that aggregates per-account instead of per-token. If that solves it we can push a targeted hotfix.

maya: are there any billing flags we should enable so we don't bill failed calls? ops-bot help?

ops-bot: billing: failed 4xx responses are excluded from consumption meter; 5xx are sometimes reprocessed. 429s are recorded as rejected and not billed by default, but we'll verify logs for that customer's reported IDs.

sam: quick win: I'll offer them a temporary support override (2x burst for 48h) and coordinate with billing to confirm no charges for rejected calls. Please capture the experiment logs so we can link evidence in the ticket.

ajay: long-term items: 1) make rate-limiter account-aware (aggregate tokens under account fallback), 2) add a guard to auth flow to prevent transient 401->retry storms, 3) update defaults for burst/window sizes based on lab findings and publish a recommended playbook for customers that rotate tokens frequently.

lina: adding checklist to the runbook: reproduce in lab (k6), confirm 429 vs 401 chain, try per-account aggregation, measure p95 improvement, propose default set. I'll paste results here when done.

maya: thanks everyone — i'll update the customer with temporary bump and ask for their logs. followups in this thread. :thumbsup:
